pages.text: Collectors around a star reach the temperature where they radiate what they absorb: 394 K/√(r/AU) for a flat absorber. They run heat engines into your coolant, so Carnot sets the efficiency: closer is hotter and better, until the collectors melt.
$(thing)Set$(): Orbit radius, Pointing duty.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Stellar flare activity: collector temperature varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Collectors melting; Heat sink as hot as the collectors: no engine can run.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Generator output follows the useful flux.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Collector temperature: T = (L/(4πr²σ))^(1/4)$(br)Stellar flux: F = L/(4πr²)$(br)Carnot efficiency: η = 1 − T_cold/T_hot$(br)Useful flux: F·duty·η
